channel.title: Palm Coast Observer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Palm Coast Observer (observerlocalnews.com)

item.title: The Observer — in your mailbox?
item.description: New 'delivery sponsorships' represent a significant shift in the Observer's distribution.

item.title: Volusia County School Board member Jamie Haynes earns distinction
item.description: Haynes was recognized with the Advanced Certified Board Member by Florida School Boards Association.

item.title: Events calendar: Attend the 12th annual Granada Grand Festival of the Arts in Ormond Beach
item.description: What to do this week in Ormond Beach and Palm Coast.

item.title: Brush fire in Flagler County that prompted evacuations is 80% contained
item.description: The fire reached an estimated 170 acres in size. Though no buildings were damaged, the flames came within 30 feet of the Baptist church on Old Dixie Highway.

item.title: Vacant Halifax Plantation school site to be sold, future use needs Volusia's approval
item.description: The school site, located on the north side of the intersection at Acoma Drive and Monaghan Drive, is under contract with a real estate development company.

item.title: Daytona Beach Commission agrees: No toilet to tap water for Daytona Beach
item.description: In a unanimous vote, the commission asked the city attorney to draft an ordinance that would ban blackwater from city potable water.

item.title: City Commissioner asks for LED lighting, new signage at Ormond Beach Sports Complex
item.description: Commissioner Kristin Deaton asked for input on adding LED lights to fields 11 and 12 following a recent fight between teens at the sports complex.

item.title: Buddy Taylor Middle School student arrested for written threats to kill or do bodily harm
item.description: The incident was the second in two days that a Flagler County middle school student was arrested for making a shooting threat.

item.title: Volusia School Board members voice opposition to SB 1620
item.description: School Board members cited lack of 'safeguards' for student, staff personal information. Bill co-sponsors Sen. Tom Leek and Sen. Don Gaetz say the bill isn't specifically targeting Volusia.

item.title: Will Flagler County continue to its portion of the lifeguard program? Flagler Beach wants to know
item.description: Flagler County paid $106,000 to the program in the 2026 budget. Whether it will continue to do so in the future, will depend on the budget numbers.
